causal_interpretation.consistent_hypothesis: Deterministic process allocation and GC cadence plausibly explain why a similar historical pause recurred at one planned position, but original sessions contain no GC callbacks and cannot be retrospectively proven.
causal_interpretation.directly_supported: The observed generation-2 collectors cause most of the latency in four newly instrumented long passes, and the external-collection control keeps its explicitly forced collections outside online timers.
not_established: The fingerprint closure cycle is the sole or dominant source of heap garbage.
The old uninstrumented HGAM spike is definitively a GC pause.
Changing only the fingerprint helper eliminates long-run major GC.
The instrumented/control timings replace either original frozen benchmark, or invalidate every original approximately 9-percent primary benefit.

limitations: Callbacks and wrappers perturb allocation and timing; not replacement benchmarks.
Default short replay does not reproduce the original preceding allocation history.
Prefix replay preserves workload order; instrumentation can move GC cadence.
Controls follow the automatic phase; phase order and heap history can confound them.
Collect-between-passes moves cyclic collection; reference counting remains.
Host spans measure enqueue work and existing waits, not GPU kernel times.
Absence of a pause in a short control does not establish its cause.
The automatic prefix covers all size-32 and size-128 source queries but only size-512 batches 0 through 5; controls cover only batches 3, 4 and 5.
Instrumented prefix and short controls have unequal durations and different heap histories; controls follow automatic collection and the acyclic phase follows 405 explicit full collections.
Two original benchmark sessions did not record GC events, so the original exact spike cause remains an inference.
CPU proof establishes a fingerprint reference cycle, while the actual trace does not report collected object types and cannot attribute all garbage to that helper.
measured_findings: Four generation-2 collections directly overlap four approximately 250-ms online passes in the automatic/original instrumented prefix. The recorded GC durations account for most of those individual timed pauses.
The long measured collections occur in sampling or feature gathering and affect blocks, HGAM and reference modes; they are not specific to HGAM message passing.
The historical exact batch/repeat/seed/fingerprint position does not spike in this diagnostic: HGAM is 28.770413 ms with zero recorded GC overlap in the automatic/original phase.

The collect-between-passes intervention performs 405 generation-2 collections entirely outside the frozen executor timers, relocating about 88.656 seconds of GC work rather than removing that wall-clock work.
The three later acyclic-hash cases retain exact archived sampler fingerprints and show no generation-2 or >100-ms online pause; generation-0/1 collection remains present.
Two early >100-ms online observations have zero GC overlap and must not be labeled GC pauses.
scope: Independent CPU-only integrity and exact raw GC-trace audit of an actual hosted instrumented NVIDIA T4 diagnostic. No new model evaluation, GPU run, or source modification performed by this audit.
